newsitem.title: USA: Northrup King Bt corn gets Japanese feed clearance.
newsitem.headline: Northrup King Bt corn gets Japanese feed clearance.

text.p: Northrup King, a unit of Sandoz AG, said Wednesday that Japan's Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Fisheries granted livestock feed clearance for its genetically enhanced Bt corn.
Northrup said the clearance brings it one step closer to Japanese approval to import the Bt corn.
Clearance by the ministry comes after an eight-month review of the product.

Previously, the Japanese Ministry of Health and Welfare allowed use of Bt corn in food and food additives. Environmental approal is expected soon, which will be the final step in the Japanese approval process, Northrup said.
Northrup King president Ed Shonsey said Japan imported nearly 635 million bushels of U.S. corn last year, making it the largest customer for American corn farmers.
"Today's approval by the Japanese once again reaffirms the safety of our Bt corn and brings us one step closer to delivering this grain to U.S. export customers," he said in a statement.
Northrup's Bt corn is genetically enhanced to be resistant to the European corn borer. The seed is currently for sale in the United States for spring planting in 1997.
Earlier this year, Northrup's Bt hybrids received approval for unrestricted sale and use in the U.S. and Canada.
Review of its Bt corn by the European Union is underway and proceeding as expected, it added.
